title: Identity reinforcement and professional confidence
definition: The product lets its user act as the professional they are (owner, operator, analyst), in their own vocabulary, with the capability a larger organisation would have, and without condescension or ceremony.
intended_outcome: A user can do real work in their own terms and hand the result to a colleague, customer or regulator without apology or rework.
implementation_guidance: Use the user's domain vocabulary in labels, errors and help. Keep a glossary file in the product repository and check labels against it.
Every artefact a user may show to others (report, export, invoice, certificate) is presentable by default: correct units, currency and locale, printable, no obstructive watermark.
Offer the full capability to every size of business. Gate on what is needed to operate (a permission), not on how large or experienced the customer appears.
Do not use diminishing copy ("simple", "even beginners"). Say what the user can now do.
Show the user's own context (company, role) in persistent chrome where the platform holds it.

automated: String scan of user-facing copy against the profile banned_phrases.
expert_review: Copy audit for condescension and vocabulary fit against the product glossary.
Export walk-through: could the owner hand this to a third party unchanged?
customer_feedback: Ask users whether they would show the output to a client or supervisor.

limitations: Professional confidence is an internal construct. No validated measure of it is used here.
What counts as presentable differs by sector and country.

evidence.summary: The owner directs that small-business owners must feel respected and equipped with sophisticated tools regardless of company size.
Presentable output and domain vocabulary make users more willing to rely on the product for work they are accountable for.
evidence.rationale: Plausible from how work artefacts are used, but untested here.
